fill.seg: And which women of noble bloud, and great estate, Semper in coniunctionibus non solum quid liceat considerandum est, sed & quid honestum sit. Digest. lib. 23. tit. 2. §. 42. make with their seruingmen. Doe they not herein bewray much basenesse of minde, and violence of lusts?
fill.p: If it be said that such mariages are not simply vnlawfull, the rule of the ciuill law giueth a good answer, Alwaies in mariages not only what is lawfull, but what is honest and meet, is to be considered.

div.head: §. 11. Of equality in piety and religion betwixt those that are to be maried together.
div.p: 4. The parity which is of greatest consequence betwixt 4. Equality in piety. parties to be maried, is in piety. In which respect it is requisite that as a Christian be maried to a Christian, and a professor of E domibus Christianis coniugij quaeratur copula. Ambr. Epist. 70. the true faith to a professor of the same faith; so one that in truth feareth God, to one of the same minde and disposition, as it is noted of Zachary and Elizabeth, they were both righteous before God, &c. A worthy couple: one worthy of another: being both alike in such excellent qualities, they could Luk. 1. 6. not but reape each from other much comfort, and profit euery way.
This is one of the most principall points that are comprised vnder that prouiso giuen by the holy Ghost in choosing a yoake fellow, in these words, In the Lord. 1 Cor. 7. 39.

There is no such meanes to increase loue, preserue peace, prouoke vnto all dutie, make helpfull one to another in all things, and at all times, as this paritie. Hereby shall they be made both able to doe more good one to another, and capeable to receiue more good one from another: especially in the best things, euen in those which concerne their spirituall edification in this world, and eternall saluation in the world to come. For Christ is the fountaine and head of all spirituall life and grace, (it pleased the father that in him should all fulnesse Col. 1. 19. dwell: so as it is he that filleth all in all things.) Now Christ communicateth Eph. 1. 23. that life and grace which is in him to those that are members of his bodie: If then I being a member of that mysticall body, be linked by that neare and inuiolable bond of mariage to one of the members of that body, what hope is there of mutuall communicating one to another, and mutuall partaking one from another of those gifts and graces which
either of vs receiue from Christ our head? If an vnbeleeuing wife may be saued by a beleeuing husband, and an vnbeleeuing 1 Cor. 1. 16. husband by a beleeuing wife: much more will one beleeuer be more and more edified by another.

Happie is that family where both the gouernours thereof husband and wife are mutuall members of Christs bodie: there will the house be made Gods Church, as the house of Aquila and Priscilla was. Gods worship will there be maintained. Rom. 16. 5. Children will there be trained vp in the nurture of the Lord: and seruants also taught the feare of God: for they that are indeed of Christs kingdome, will be as leuen which Mat. 13. 33. seasoneth the whole lumpe: instance the profession which Iosuah Ios. 24. 15. maketh to this purpose: and the effect which is noted of the ruler whose sonne Christ cured, he himselfe beleeued and Ioh. 4. 53. his whole house.

Here by the way, let me exhort parents & other gouernours Exhortation to marie in the Lord. See Treat. 3. §. 68. of children, both to traine vp their owne children in true piety & feare of God, and also to seeke such matches for them, as they may haue some assurance that they are of the same faith, and of the same minde and heart: thus shall they procure to their children much happinesse in their mariage as Abraham did to Isaak, Gen. 24.

If parents ought in this respect to procure the good of their children, much more ought they who are of themselues, and haue liberty to marie with whom they will, haue an especiall respect to parity in piety: especially femals, because they are in subiection to their husbands: yet ought not men to be carelesse herein: for wiues, if the feare of God possesse not their hearts, though they be the weaker vessels, doe oft make their husbands plaine vassals to them.

div.head: §. 12. Of mariages betwixt persons of diuers professions.
div.p: Contrary are mariages with persons of different dispositions, and Deut. 7. 3. Neh. 10. 30. diuers professions in religion: especially when they are made with infidels or idolaters.
This is one of those vnequall yoakes, wherewith 2 Cor. 6. 14. the Apostle Dammages of vnequall matches in religion. forbiddeth Christians to be yoaked.

Great are the dangers and dammages that ordinarily fall out thereupon. For first the Ezr. 9. 2. holy seed (to vse the words of the holy
Ghost) is thereby mixed: whereby it commeth to passe that Mal. 2. 11. the holinesse of the Lord is profaned, that is, they whom God hath chosen to be an holy nation, and a peculiar people to him, are polluted.

p.hi: The vnbeleeuing husband is sanctified by the wife, and the vnbeleeuing wife by the husband.

div.p: Answ. That is noted only as a remedy of an inconuenience, which being fallen out cannot be recalled: as when two infidels being maried together, the one of them is conuerted to the true faith and the other remaineth an infidell, that the beleeuer might with some comfort enioy the company of the Non de ijs qui adhuc coniuncti non sunt, sed de coniunctis agitur. Siquidem non dicit si quis vult accipere infidelem, sed si quis habet infidelem. Chrysost. in 1 Cor. 7. hom. 19. other, the Apostle sheweth that for matrimoniall communion the vnbeleeuer is sanctified by the beleeuer. But hereby he giueth no liberty to beleeuers to marie with vnbeleeuers. For though God in mercy thus sanctifie the vnequall yoake which cannot be broken, yet they who professing Gods name doe wittingly vndergoe that yoake, doe as much as in them lieth, profane Gods holinesse.

2. The professor of the true religion is thereby in danger of Apostasie. Which reason Deut. 7. 4. the law it selfe presseth against this point: and the Scripture giueth many examples of the wofull issue thereof: as of 1 King. 11. 4. Salomon the wisest among men, Iudg. 16. 16. of Sampson the strongest, of 2 King. 8. 18. Iehoram and others.
Obiect. If I marie one of a contrary religion, I may conuert a sinner from going astray, and saue a soule from death.

Answ. It is but a meere may, thou hast no warrant to make that venture, but art forbid to auoid the contrary danger. There is great cause of feare that in an vnequall yoake the worse will preuaile ouer the better. We are naturally prone to yeeld to error, falshood, and all manner of euill. Truth, vertue and grace, are against the current of nature. It is like to fall out in this vnequall yoake, as if two oxen should in one yoake draw contrarie waies one against the other on the side of an hill; that oxe which draweth downe-hill, though it be a poore, leane, weake one, will draw downe the other, though it should be an able, lusty, strong one. All euill is downe hill: all goodnesse is vp hill: and by reason of the flesh which remaineth in all, so long as they remaine on earth, they who
haue some goodnesse in them are prone and ready to fall away: but they which are euill are very obstinate therein. Yea euill also is of a more spreading and infecting nature. A little sowre leauen will soone make a great batch of dough sowre: but a great deale of sweet dough will not sweeten a little leauen. It is therefore an vnwarrantable pretext for any to marie one of a contrarie religion, or disposition, on hope to conuert them. It is not in mans power to conuert another. It is a diuine worke, without Gods blessing it cannot be done. Little ground there is to expect a blessing from God in that course which is directly against his owne ordinance. A curse may rather be feared. And wofull experience of all ages hath shewed how God hath cursed such mariages.

Obiect. Saint 1 Pet. 3. 1. Peter exhorteth wiues so to carrie themselues, as their husbands, which obey not the word, may by that meanes be won without the word, and 1 Cor. 7. 16. Saint Paul saith to such as were vnequally matched, what knowest thou, ô wife, whether thou shalt saue thy husband? or how knowest thou, ô man, whether thou shalt saue thy wife? It appeareth therefore that an euill husband may be conuerted by a good wife: and an euill wife by a good husband.

Ans. These directions are noted only as a remedie to redresse such irreuocable mischiefes as are fallen out, and not to giue libertie of rushing wittingly into them (as was before noted.) When an ill euent is fallen out, necessity lieth on a man; so as all meanes is to be vsed to redresse the same. But thereupon to inferre that a man may safely enter into that course which draweth a man to those mischiefes, what is it but to thrust himselfe into the fire, and to cast himselfe into temptation, Mat. 6. 13. which he is taught to pray against? besides, the forenamed directions are not grounded on any expresse promises, but vpon meere suppositions.
3. Many other mischiefes are like to follow vpon this kinde of vnequall mariage, besides danger of apostasie (which yet is the greatest) as

1. Nihil grauius quam copulari alienigenae, vbi discordiae incentiua conflantur. Ambr. Ep. 70. Many iars and contentions betwixt man and wife. For how can there be mutuall mariage-concord, betwixt those that are of different mindes?
2. Disturbance of the family: one part holding with the man, another with the woman.
3. Wasting of goods: the husband spending what he can on such as are of his profession: and the wife what she can, on them that are of hers.

4. Hinderance of all holy duties in the house: the partie that is of Cum oratio communis esse debeat, quomodo inter dispares deuotione potest esse coniugij communis charitas? Ibid. the contrarie profession not enduring that there should be any.

5. Profanenesse and Atheisme in children. For commonly when parents are of diuers religions, children are of none: Leu. 24. 10, 11. instance that cursed blasphemer, whose mother was an Israelite, but his father an Egyptian.
The Scripture noteth such children to be Gen. 6. 4. monsters, and Neh. 13. 24. mongrels.
Obiect. Salmon maried Mat. 1. 5. Rahab, and Booz maried Ruth, both which women were infidels.

Answ. They had beene so, but were not so when they maried them. Faith and repentance, as they alter the disposition, so also the condition of the worst that can be. Ios. 2. 9, &c. Heb. 11. 31. Rahabs faith was manifested before she was maried to Salmon: and Ruth 1. 16. Ruth had forsaken her country gods, and chosen the God of Israel to be her God: and Ruth 2. 11, 12. Booz knew as much.
Obiect. But no such thing can be said of the Iudg. 14. 1, &c. daughter of the Philistims whom Sampson maried.

Answ. This was an extraordinary matter, and therefore not examplarie for all. That he did it by an extraordinarie instinct is euident by this phrase, it was of the Lord: that it is not examplarie is euident, because Deut. 7. 3. Gods law, the rule of example, forbids it. God moued him thereto to manifest his owne power and wisdome thereby.

His power, in that he was able to worke by contraries: as to worke enmity by amity; vtter destruction by neere coniunction: for God turned the heart of Sampson, a chiefe man in Israel, to affect, and desire in mariage, a daughter of the Philistims: and moued the parents of that maid to giue her to Sampson in mariage: here was amity and neere coniunction. Yet Iudg. 15. the history sheweth that by this meanes an occasion was giuen to Sampson to reuenge himselfe, and the people of God on the Philistims.

His Wisdome, in that he turned that which had an apparent shew of great euill, into much good. For, that Sampson a Nazarit of the Lord, a chiefe man in Israel, should ioyne in mariage with a daughter of idolaters, who also were spightfull enemies of the Lords people, caried a shew of euill to such as knew not the spirit of Sampson, nor the intent of the Lord: yet God by this meanes brought Sampson to be a Iudge and deliuerer of his people.

By such a spirit as Eliah called for fire from heauen, did 2 King. 1. 10. Sampson marrie an idolater. If any hence shall thinke of marying Idolaters, I may say to them as Christ to his disciples, ye know not of what spirit ye are. This example of Sampson can Luk 9. 55. be no more warrant to others to marie with idolaters, then his practise in pulling downe an house on his head, to selfe-murtherers. Iudg. 16. 30. The warrant of extraordinarie matters is particular, proper and peculiar to them only that doe them. But the warrant of exemplary matters must be the generall and knowne will of God in his word.
Whether in some particular cases this generall rule may be dispensed withall or not, I leaue to the determination of more learned Diuines, and submit all to the iudgement of Gods Church.

div.head: §. 13. Of that mutuall liking which must passe betwixt mariageable persons before they be maried.
div.p: Hauing shewed what persons are fit to be ioyned in mariage, it remaineth, to shew after what manner they are to be ioyned.
There are in Scripture three steps or degrees commended vnto vs by which mariageable parties are in order to proceed vnto mariage.
1. A mutuall liking.
2. An actuall contract.
3. A publike solemnization of mariage.

I. The first liking is sometimes on the parents or other friends part, and then by them made knowne to the partie to be maried, as the friends of Rebeca, liking the offer of Isaak Gen. 24. 58. which was made by Abrahams seruant, made it knowne to Rebeca her selfe.
